concerns.text: The validation signature is derived from GSE138852 responder vs. non-responder labels, but the plan does not state that GSE138852 is EXCLUDED from fork-point-gene discovery. If fork-point genes are discovered in all four datasets (discovery_dataset_ids is plural and includes GSE138852 by default), then enrichment of those genes against a signature computed from differential expression in the SAME dataset is partially circular: highly variable exhaustion-associated genes will appear in both the fork-point list and the response signature for reasons unrelated to the trajectory claim. Specify a discovery/validation split (discover in GSE136103/127465/111075, validate only in GSE138852), or justify same-dataset enrichment.

FR-008 mandates validation against an INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED therapy-response signature (PMID 32012345, 'derived from a separate cohort and thus provides an unbiased validation set'). The plan replaces this with a signature computed from GSE138852's own response labels. This weakens the independence the spec's validation logic depends on (Constitution VI explicitly requires validation against PUBLISHED signatures). Either use the published gene set as the primary enrichment target (with the GSE138852-label signature as secondary), or document why the published set is unavailable and obtain spec-level sign-off on the substitution.

Spearman correlation of timing ranks for the 'top 3' genes is statistically degenerate: with n=3, Spearman takes only a few discrete values and ≥0.80 essentially forces identical ordering. The plan reports it 'as measured' (good), but should note this is a near-tautological check at n=3 and pre-specify the interpretation (e.g., report correlation over all shared fork-point genes, with top-3 as a spec-mandated subset).
